blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      validation-checks: '["agents-suite","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-suite/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check — a red shard fails this job through `needs`.
    needs: [static, test]
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: count-*
          path: shard-counts
      - name: Merge shard coverage
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq lcov
          mkdir -p coverage
          ARGS=$(for f in coverage-shards/lcov-*/lcov.info; do printf -- '-a %s ' "$f"; done)
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          lcov $ARGS -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: Sum shard test counts
        id: counts
        run: |
          TOTAL=$(cat shard-counts/count-*/shard_count.txt | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
          echo "test_count=$TOTAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Install crap4dart
        # 0.9.5: fixed the test_assertions parser limitation with trailing
        # named `skip:` args, so the two config excludes are gone. Keep this
        # pin aligned with the version the pre-commit hook runs locally.
        run: dart pub global activate crap4dart 0.9.5
      - run: crap4dart check --all
      - run: crap4dart analyze
      - name: Generate badges
        run: |
          mkdir -p .badges
          TEST_COUNT="${{ steps.counts.outputs.test_count }}"

blocks.text:
# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Hosted here so target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) and their .dmtools/config.js — no workflow copies to drift.
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo, vars.*
# and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# What it does: installs the pinned dmtools CLI (release asset, no repo
# file needed), checks out THIS repository at the exact ref the caller
# invoked (github.workflow_ref self-pin — engine and factory always match),
# and runs the SM rule engine (smAgent.js, deterministic, no LLM) against
# the target repo's loop state.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      factory_ref:
        description: "The ref this workflow was invoked with (same literal as the stub uses-ref). GitHub exposes no context/env for the called-workflow ref (GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF is the CALLER's), so the stub passes its pin explicitly."
        required: true
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "BRIDGE-FREE MODE (owner 2026-09-23): JSON array of required check names. When set, the SM tick itself stamps these checks on PR heads (in_progress at dispatch, verdict from the newest dispatched run) — delete the repo's ci-gate bridge workflow. Example: '[\"Quality gate\",\"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)\",\"Binaries smoke gate\"]'. Empty = legacy bridge architecture."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:

          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

          # inputs or secrets (live-verified BOTH arrive empty) — but a
          # called workflow can reference its OWN github.token directly:
          # same repo, same run, pushes with it trigger no workflows.

          repo='${{ github.repository }}'

          if [ -n "$SILENT_GH_TOKEN" ]; then
            extra=",\"silentToken\":\"${SILENT_GH_TOKEN}\",\"sourceToken\":\"${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN}\""
          fi
          # #687: machine login is deployment-level (never hardcoded in the
          # agents repo) — jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor.

          # array as a STRING jobParam — escaped for the override JSON).
          vc='${{ inputs.validation-checks }}'
          if [ -n "$vc" ]; then
            vc_escaped=$(printf '%s' "$vc" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
            extra="${extra},\"validationChecks\":\"${vc_escaped}\""

          # uploads a factory-state.json snapshot as a release asset; the
          # board reads the public CDN link (no tokens, no rate limits).
          sp='${{ inputs.state-publish }}'

            sp_escaped=$(printf '%s' "$sp" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')

          # Parallel read fan-out (OPT-IN, dmtools Dart runtime only): a
          # value parsing to int >= 2 wires the runAsync worker pool into

        required: false

        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows.         required: false

        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false

  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Quirky but correct; each stub matches its callee.
6. ✅ No secrets/log changes; no injection surface (static config value, repo-controlled).

Also there's a subtle cross-repo contract: `validation-checks` names must match quality.yml job names; `machine-merge.yml`'s `workflow_run: workflows: ['Quality']` must match quality.yml's `name: Quality`. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.
Let me read the input files now.

{"path":"input/pr-304/ticket.md"}

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@0c19a4fe26dc36672bf80193f91ff38d96c82ad2
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      validation-checks: '["agents-suite","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-suite/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check — a red shard fails this job through `needs`.
    needs: [static, test]
    runs-on: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
    steps:
      - name: Runner disk hygiene
        # Bitrise pool machines accumulate per-run workdirs; twice on
        # 2026-09-26 a full disk killed agents-suite mid-run. Drop stale
        # dirs (>1 day) before checkout. Never touches the current
        # workspace; fresh mtimes protect concurrently running jobs.
        run: |
          df -h / || true
          WS_PARENT="$(dirname "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          CUR="$(basename "$RUNNER_WORKSPACE")"
          find "$WS_PARENT" -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name "$CUR" -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find "$WS_PARENT/_temp" -mindepth 1 -mtime +1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h / || true
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: count-*
          path: shard-counts
      - name: Merge shard coverage
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq lcov
          mkdir -p coverage
          ARGS=$(for f in coverage-shards/lcov-*/lcov.info; do printf -- '-a %s ' "$f"; done)
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          lcov $ARGS -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: Sum shard test counts
        id: counts
        run: |
          TOTAL=$(cat shard-counts/count-*/shard_count.txt | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
          echo "test_count=$TOTAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Install crap4dart
        # 0.9.5: fixed the test_assertions parser limitation with trailing
        # named `skip:` args, so the two config excludes are gone. Keep this
        # pin aligned with the version the pre-commit hook runs locally.
        run: dart pub global activate crap4dart 0.9.5
      - run: crap4dart check --all
      - run: crap4dart analyze
      - name: Generate badges
        run: |
          mkdir -p .badges
          TEST_COUNT="${{ steps.counts.outputs.test_count }}"

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Hosted here so target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) and their .dmtools/config.js — no workflow copies to drift.
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo, vars.*
# and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# What it does: installs the pinned dmtools CLI (release asset, no repo
# file needed), checks out THIS repository at the exact ref the caller
# invoked (github.workflow_ref self-pin — engine and factory always match),
# and runs the SM rule engine (smAgent.js, deterministic, no LLM) against
# the target repo's loop state.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      factory_ref:
        description: "The ref this workflow was invoked with (same literal as the stub uses-ref). GitHub exposes no context/env for the called-workflow ref (GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF is the CALLER's), so the stub passes its pin explicitly."
        required: true
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "BRIDGE-FREE MODE (owner 2026-09-23): JSON array of required check names. When set, the SM tick itself stamps these checks on PR heads (in_progress at dispatch, verdict from the newest dispatched run) — delete the repo's ci-gate bridge workflow. Example: '[\"Quality gate\",\"JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)\",\"Binaries smoke gate\"]'. Empty = legacy bridge architecture."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — GitHub API access for the SM engine (labels, PR state, checks, dispatch). secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries, so the stub passes it explicitly.'
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "The caller workflow's github.token — pushes made with it trigger NO workflows, so silent branch updates (#687) refresh armed PRs without re-running the CI matrix. Optional: without it updates use the PAT (CI re-runs)."
        required: false

# Never two SM instances; never cancel an in-flight reconcile. The caller
# stub declares the same group — combined, still one tick at a time.
concurrency:
  group: machine-sm
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read          # checkout target + engine
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  reconcile:
    # Runner is caller-controlled: `runner` input, default hosted ubuntu.
    # epam-org callers (dmtools-dart) pass bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci — the
    # Bitrise Build Hub pool the Java repo uses (probe epam/dmtools-dart#229:
    # 15s pickup). IstiN-org callers CANNOT see that pool (fa tick
    # 35864581472 queued 4+ min with no runner) and use the default.
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve factory ref (self-pin)
        # github.workflow_ref = "<owner>/<repo>/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>"
        # — the engine is checked out at EXACTLY the ref the caller invoked,
        # so rules and workflow can never skew apart.
        run: echo "FACTORY_REF=${{ inputs.factory_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: "Checkout factory (dmtools-agents: SM engine + rules)"
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: IstiN/dmtools-agents
          ref: ${{ env.FACTORY_REF }}
          path: factory-agents
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.16' }}

run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Reconcile the machine loop
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          # dmtools reads SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (env-parity with Java); without
          # it the GitHub integration counts as unconfigured and the JS
          # runtime does not expose github_* globals at all.
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # github.token does NOT cross the reusable-call boundary through
          # inputs or secrets (live-verified BOTH arrive empty) — but a
          # called workflow can reference its OWN github.token directly:
          # same repo, same run, pushes with it trigger no workflows.
          SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.silent-token || secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          repo='${{ github.repository }}'
          # #687: silentToken powers update_branch localActions (github.token
          # pushes trigger no workflows); sourceToken restores the PAT after.
          extra=""
          if [ -n "$SILENT_GH_TOKEN" ]; then
            extra=",\"silentToken\":\"${SILENT_GH_TOKEN}\",\"sourceToken\":\"${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN}\""
          fi
          # #687: machine login is deployment-level (never hardcoded in the
          # agents repo) — jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor.
          ma='${{ inputs.machine-author }}'
          if [ -n "$ma" ]; then
            extra="${extra},\"machineAuthor\":\"${ma}\""
          fi
          # Dispatch-only CI: which workflow file the SM runs on PR heads.
          cw='${{ inputs.ci-workflow }}'
          if [ -n "$cw" ]; then
            extra="${extra},\"ciWorkflow\":\"${cw}\""
          fi
          # Bridge-free mode: check names the tick stamps itself (JSON
          # array as a STRING jobParam — escaped for the override JSON).
          vc='${{ inputs.validation-checks }}'
          if [ -n "$vc" ]; then
            vc_escaped=$(printf '%s' "$vc" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
            extra="${extra},\"validationChecks\":\"${vc_escaped}\""
          fi
          # Factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23, OPT-IN): JSON object
          # {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. Empty = off. The tick
          # uploads a factory-state.json snapshot as a release asset; the
          # board reads the public CDN link (no tokens, no rate limits).
          sp='${{ inputs.state-publish }}'
          if [ -n "$sp" ]; then
            sp_escaped=$(printf '%s' "$sp" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
            extra="${extra},\"statePublish\":\"${sp_escaped}\""
          fi
          # Parallel read fan-out (OPT-IN, dmtools Dart runtime only): a
          # value parsing to int >= 2 wires the runAsync worker pool into
          # the SM engine (parallel enrichment/probes). '0'/absent =
          # sequential fallback — the override gains nothing, exactly like
          # the pre-knob behavior.
          pw='${{ inputs.parallel-workers }}'
          if [ -n "$pw" ]; then
            pw_int=$(printf '%s' "$pw" | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' || true)
            if [ -n "$pw_int" ] && [ "$pw_int" -ge 2 ]; then

# Machine SM factory leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agentic-workflows:
# the frozen machine-loop home. GitHub requires reusable workflows at the
# .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# Migrated from IstiN/dmtools-agents factory-sm.yml (f377609) — the
# agents-repo copy is DEPRECATED for new callers (kept only so existing
# pinned users like fa keep resolving their historical SHA).
#
# FREEZE CONTRACT: target repositories carry only a thin stub (schedule +
# this call) pinned to an immutable SHA of THIS repo. Agent code and the
# dmtools CLI are NOT tied to that SHA anymore — they resolve from RELEASES
# by version knobs (repo variables of the CALLER, per-repo, no workflow
# edits to bump):
#
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION   — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' or e.g.
#                           'agents-rel-20260928-…'); the agent pack
#                           (sm_github) is fetched from that release's
#                           asset catalog via the dmtools registry
#                           (DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY). Default: latest.
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION  — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' or
#                           'vX.Y.Z'); installed from the release bundle.
#                           Default: latest.
#
# Runs in the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo,
# vars.* and secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own
# versions).
#
# What it does: resolves the two version knobs, installs the dmtools CLI
# (release asset, no repo file needed), then runs the SM rule engine as a
# VERSIONED AGENT PACK (dmtools run sm_github@latest) against the target
# repo's loop state — the pack carries smAgent.js + rules + engine closure,
# verified against the release's sha256 inventory.
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     schedule: [{cron: '*/10 * * * *'}]
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {dryRun: {type: boolean, default: true}}}
#   jobs:
#     sm:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}   # STRING —
#         # typed (boolean) reusable inputs reject expressions; strings take them.
#       secrets:
#         SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Factory · Machine SM'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      dryRun:
        description: "'true' to log the plan without acting (STRING — boolean-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions, live bisect probes D/E)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'false'
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login for #687 PR rules: excluded from review-external-once, gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews and the SM prMachineAuthor rules (auto legs, e.g. auto rework). Global-level knob — the agents repo carries no hardcoded login."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      silent-token:
        description: "The caller's github.token for silent branch updates (#687) — pushes with it trigger no workflows. Routed as an INPUT: GitHub delivers an EMPTY value when github.token is mapped through the reusable-call secrets block (live-verified), while inputs carry it; GitHub auto-masks token values in logs either way."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      ci-workflow:
        description: "CI workflow FILE NAME the SM dispatches on PR heads (dispatch-only CI: pushes fire no CI). Per-repo knob — e.g. 'quality.yml' (dmtools-dart) vs 'ci.yml' (fa). Rides jobParams.ciWorkflow into the SM engine."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: 'quality.yml'
      validation-checks:
        description: "Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps these check names itself. JSON array as a STRING (e.g. '[\"agents-suite\",\"static\",\"gate\"]')."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      parallel-workers:
        description: "OPT-IN (dmtools Dart runtime only): runAsync worker-pool size for parallel READ fan-out inside the SM tick (per-PR/issue enrichment, dispatched-CI probes). '0'/absent = runAsync not wired — the engine takes its sequential fallback (Java/GraalJS parity), zero deviation. A value parsing to int >= 2 rides jobParams.parallelWorkers."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: '0'
      state-publish:
        description: "OPT-IN factory-state publishing (owner 2026-09-23): JSON object {channel:'release', repo?, tag?, asset?}. The tick uploads factory-state.json as a public prerelease asset; the board (site/factory) reads the releases/latest CDN link. Empty = off."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

# EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the callee
# does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing declared one fails
# the guard test (factory_stub_ref_test.dart parity in each caller).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: "PAT for GitHub tool calls + gh CLI (SM engine + validation probes)."
        required: true
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN:
        description: "Optional dedicated silent-update token; the silent-token input wins when both are set."
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

env:
  # Version knobs resolve from the CALLER's repository variables (vars.*
  # resolve in the caller's context for reusable workflows) — bumping an
  # agent/CLI version is a repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
  AGENTS_VERSION: ${{ vars.AGENTS_VERSION || 'latest' }}
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'latest' }}

jobs:
  sm:
    name: sm / reconcile
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The pack runner resolves .dmtools/config.js from the CWD —
          # the target repo root (machineAuthor, jira.fields, ...).
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve versions (agents release + dmtools CLI)
        # 'latest' resolves to the newest PUBLISHED release tag at tick
        # time; an explicit tag (e.g. vars.AGENTS_VERSION=agents-rel-…)
        # pins the tick reproducibly. Fails loudly when the tag does not
        # exist (gh api exits non-zero → red tick, no silent fallback).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          resolve_tag() {
            local repo="$1" knob="$2"
            if [ "$knob" = "latest" ]; then
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name
            else
              # existence check — a typo'd pin must fail HERE, not in the tick
              gh api "repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${knob}" --jq .tag_name
            fi
          }
          AGENTS_TAG="$(resolve_tag IstiN/dmtools-agents "$AGENTS_VERSION")"
          DMTOOLS_TAG="$(resolve_tag epam/dmtools-dart "$DMTOOLS_VERSION")"
          echo "AGENTS_TAG=${AGENTS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "DMTOOLS_TAG=${DMTOOLS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "agents pack release: ${AGENTS_TAG} (knob: ${AGENTS_VERSION})"
          echo "dmtools CLI release: ${DMTOOLS_TAG} (knob: ${DMTOOLS_VERSION})"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_TAG}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_TAG}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

        C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"]
        C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"]
        C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"]
        C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"]
    end

    USE --> SAFETY
    SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN
    SAFETY --> EXAMPLES
    SAFETY --> CWD
```
